author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The White House is considering whether to use the Defense Production Act to expand U.S. oil-refining capacity as elevated fuel costs increase pressure on the domestic energy system, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. No final decision has been made, and further talks with refiners are expected.

The discussions are focused on improving efficiency and adding capacity at existing facilities rather than relying only on the construction of entirely new refineries, which can take years and require large capital commitments. Reuters reported that U.S. refining utilization has been running near 98%, leaving limited room to increase output through higher operating rates alone.

The administration is also evaluating permitting changes, regulatory steps and investment incentives. The Defense Production Act can give the federal government tools to prioritize contracts and support production considered important to national security, but any specific application to refining would depend on the policy ultimately selected. The review is developing against the backdrop of disrupted Middle East energy flows and higher transportation costs. Until an action is announced, the proposal remains one option under consideration rather than a new requirement for the industry.
dek: Officials are considering tools to improve and expand existing facilities, but Reuters reports that no final decision has been made.
headline: White House weighs Defense Production Act for refinery expansion
